title: Wright Air Development Center anti-gravity research team
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Wright Air Development Center anti-gravity research team, about 1950s at Wright Air Development Center, Dayton, Ohio, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Wright Air Development Center, Dayton, Ohio

We know that right airfield had a dedicated team of people working on anti-gravity which included Lewis Whitten father of Ed Whitten who is at Martin Corporation's RA their anti-gravity division

as_told.title: Wright Field anti-gravity team including Louis Witten and Martin's RIAS

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s the Wright Air Development Center, a US Air Force research base in Dayton, Ohio, had a team of physicists working on anti-gravity, meaning ways to cancel or control gravity. In a later episode he says the team included Louis Witten, a physicist and the father of the physicist Ed Witten, and ties him to the anti-gravity work of RIAS, a research institute run by the aircraft maker Martin Corporation. If true, it would mean the military was seriously studying gravity control decades ago.
